reference: Polymetallic massive sulfide, Potter Mine (Commons title)

description.lithology: Two intervals visible: upper dark grey to black fine-grained laminated siliceous metasediment/chert with contorted to tightly folded flow-banding, and lower 1.0 m brassy-yellow to silvery-grey and greenish fine- to medium-grained banded to massive sulfide-rich rock with relict foliation and dark siliceous bands, texture massive to semi-massive
description.alteration: weak to moderate chloritic(?) greenish tint in lower mineralized slab, otherwise none visible with certainty
description.mineralization: brassy-yellow chalcopyrite(?) +/- silvery-grey sulfides as banded semi-massive to massive mineralization comprising ~70-90 vol% of lower slab, with minor disseminated to blebby/stringer brassy sulfides ~3-7 vol% in upper dark unit

anomalies.explanation: Lower 1.0 m slab (98-01 696.9 m) displays semi-massive to massive brassy-yellow and silvery metallic sulfides over most of the exposed surface.
Upper dark grey-black laminated core shows tight contorted folding/flow-banding that should be checked for tectonic versus soft-sediment origin.
Sharp contrast between upper dark siliceous core and lower sulfide-rich slab at the divider should be checked as a lithology/mineralization contact.
